growth_story.headline: Income per person in Mauritius has grown about 3.5 percent a year since 1990 as tourism and finance took over from sugar and textiles; it is at a record high.
growth_story.arc: Since 1990, income per person in Mauritius has grown by about 3.5 percent a year, and the data show no lasting shift in that pace, so the whole period reads as one era. The World Bank ties the earlier years to export-led growth from a strong manufacturing base, with textiles and sugar as the main goods exports, which weakened after trade preferences ended in 2004, 2009 and 2017. Tourism and financial and business services took up much of the slack, and income per person grew 4.0 percent a year over 2006–2015. In 2020 the pandemic cut income per person by 14.2 percent, the deepest fall in the record, before a tourism-led recovery brought growth of 8.7 percent in 2022 and 5.9 percent in 2023. That one bad year pulls the 2016–2025 average down to 2.7 percent, yet income per person reached its highest level ever in 2025, when it grew 3.3 percent. The World Bank now describes growth as led by consumption and public transfers, with falling investment and a fast-ageing population.

threads.text: The World Bank finds that growth now leans on household spending and on public transfers financed by borrowing, while investment has fallen and gone mostly into real estate. The population is also ageing fast, so the share of people of working age is shrinking.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank says the old export-led model is under increasing strain, but the data find no lasting break since 1990. Income per person grew 4.0 percent a year in 2006–2015 and 2.7 percent in 2016–2025, and the single fall of 2020 accounts for more than that whole gap; in 2025 income per person was at its highest level ever.
